---
title: "Set up a project"
---

These options are available in preview.6 and the matching R source package.
They are absent from preview.5.

## Start with the files you need

From the project folder, run:

~~~bash
proj --project . init
~~~

In a terminal, proj asks for a title, purpose and optional contact details. The
purpose appears near the top of README.md. Blank optional answers are skipped;
end-of-input cancels before setup starts. Existing README and metadata files are
preserved. VERSION is authoritative: its synchronization setting can update only
an existing DESCRIPTION Version when the two version values differ. Equivalent
version spellings retain their original DESCRIPTION bytes.

DESCRIPTION is optional project metadata, not an automatic R package. Request it
explicitly; this does not create R/ or NAMESPACE:

~~~bash
proj --project . --non-interactive init --description-file \
  --title "Example analysis" --purpose "Compare the two models." \
  --contact-name "Project contact" --contact-email "contact@example.invalid" \
  --git=false --github=false
~~~

If the folder name is a valid R package name it supplies Package. Otherwise that
field is omitted, rather than inventing a package identity. Other project metadata
can still be useful; adding DESCRIPTION alone does not make a valid R package.

README.md is the default. --readme-rmd explicitly chooses README.Rmd. Setup does
not render it or replace the other README format. In R, the existing generic
transport can select exactly the same CLI flags:

~~~r
projcli::proj_cli("init",
  c("--readme-rmd", "--title", "Example analysis", "--git=false", "--github=false"),
  project = ".")
~~~

Named R helpers now expose these same shared CLI actions.

## Choose Git and a remote deliberately

Interactive init asks about Git only when the folder is outside a repository.
Enclosing repositories and linked worktrees count. Any existing Git remote is
enough, regardless of host, and is never replaced.

When there is no remote, GitHub is an optional setup route using an already
installed, authenticated gh command. General init creates a private empty remote;
it does not commit or push project files. No credentials are installed or changed.
Use --git=true and --github=true only when intentionally selecting those actions.
Omitted noninteractive options skip both. The existing standalone init git/github
commands retain their separate, explicit commit/push behavior.

## Choose a code licence, or defer

The general-init choices match projr: CC-BY, Apache 2.0, CC0 and Proprietary. Choose
later to defer. Noninteractive init does not choose one for you.

~~~bash
proj --project . --non-interactive init --code-license apache
~~~

The root LICENSE notice applies to source code, not automatically to input data
or third-party material. Existing LICENSE or LICENSE.md is preserved. Public
licence texts are bundled from their publishers; Proprietary requires an explicit
copyright holder, for example --copyright-holder "Example organisation".

Folder licensing is a separate explicit operation, never a general-init loop:

~~~bash
proj --project . init license --label raw-data --license ccby
~~~

This uses a declared project-contained label, writes only that folder's missing
LICENSE and preserves existing licences. External mappings and root aliases are
not supported by label mode. It does not license sibling directories.

## Add a citation without R

Citation creation is opt-in and requires explicit authors. Contact details are
not taken as authors. No DOI, licence, dependency citations or other identifiers
are invented.

~~~bash
proj --project . --non-interactive init --citation --title "Example analysis" \
  --author-family "Example" --author-given "Ada" --author-name "Research team"
~~~

CITATION.cff uses schema1.2.0. Repeat person flags in author order; supply one given
name value per family name, or omit all given names. Team names follow person
authors. Existing CITATION.cff is preserved. This does not require cffr or any R
installation. The remote fixture validates emitted files with the
[official schema](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/tree/1.2.0).

## Initialize renv only when selected

init renv remains a separate action using already installed renv. General init
calls it only with --renv, default off. It does not restore dependencies. Existing
renv state or .Rprofile is protected by that action's existing refusal behavior.

## Inspect and preserve

proj init plan reads existing setup without creating files or contacting a server.
Machine mode returns the initialization object for frontends.

Automatic .Rbuildignore creation requires DESCRIPTION; an existing .Rbuildignore
can still retain its managed block. Generated project-control exclusions do not
exclude R/, man/ or inst/. Explicit per-directory ignore settings remain
authoritative. Paths are escaped as R regular expressions, separately from
.gitignore glob escaping. Custom rules outside the delimited managed block survive;
malformed/repeated markers fail clearly rather than accumulating new blocks.

Initialization is incremental: successful local steps remain if a later optional
renv/Git/GitHub action fails. It is not a whole-project or network transaction.
Linked/special metadata targets fail before setup writes. Repeating metadata setup
does not overwrite existing files; synchronization of a genuinely different
DESCRIPTION Version is the stated exception.


## R initialization helpers

Preview.6 adds projr_init, projr_init_plan, projr_init_readme,
projr_init_license and projr_init_renv. They use the shared CLI, with explicit R
metadata values. Only opted-in renv setup checks its optional suggested package;
installation requires interactive consent or explicit install_missing=TRUE.
See the [named R reference](../r-reference.qmd#initialization) for examples, defaults and library details.
